# A record of a generated file that a person's formatter will touch compares layout-blind structure, never exact bytes — or the formatter makes an untouched file look edited

In a-new-project-starts-instrumented the scaffold recorded a sha256 of the exact text of each file it wrote. The scaffold installs Biome (lineWidth 100); Biome reflowed the one-line rendered settings object, so every later `update` found the file differing from its record and wrote the template beside it, and a daemon address reset never reached the app. The cold audit reproduced it on the seat-holds demo. Rule: when InDusk records generated files that the project's own tools (formatters, linters) rewrite, the record must compare something layout-blind (a fingerprint with whitespace, semicolons, trailing commas and quote style ignored), keep reading older exact-text records, and the plan must name the formatter in the test (T31 reformats the way Biome prints). Alternative the audit left open: a format-ignore comment on the generated line. See .indusk/planning/archive/a-new-project-starts-instrumented (Build Phase 5) and /decisions/init-sets-up-telemetry.
